newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds ended softer on Tuesday as investor sentiment turned twitchy after worse-than-expected private sector credit data late on Monday and concerns about the rand.
At 1415 GMT government's benchmark R150 bond was at 14.13 percent from an intraday high of 14.18 percent and 14.01 percent at the previous local close.
"Bond yields started climbing last night on the credit number which was negative," said a debt trader at a foreign bank, noting that the rand had tracked bonds weaker.

The Reserve Bank said on Monday that private sector credit extension rose 16.39 percent in June -- well above Reuters' consensus forecast of a 15.19 percent year-on-year rise -- which dealers said had diminished hopes for an early cut in interest rates.
"The CPI figure then came out today, which was positive, and yields started falling but the rand continued to weaken and the bond market retraced, on nervousness over the rand."
South Africa's annual consumer price inflation rate fell to a nine-month low of 8.8 percent in June, beating economists' expectations of a 9.1 percent year-on-year rise.
Traders said the positive CPI figure and trade data -- a 4.149 billion rand surplus in June from 1.75 billion rand surplus in May -- were not enough to balance out the poor credit figure.
"What it means is that an interest rate cut will probably be delayed until the next (July) credit figures are released by the Reserve Bank," the trader said.
On Wednesday, he expected benchmark gilts to trade in a 14.05 to 14.14 percent range as players would likely avoid going long.
"Bonds have overrun themselves a bit and I'm not expecting too much tomorrow," he said.
Foreigners bought a net 269.30 million rands worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 569.69 million on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover was at 3.48 billion rand on Monday from 7.23 billion rand on Friday.
The rand repeated Monday's pattern, hit early in the morning by importer dollar demand and weakening to a 4.5920 bid before some profit-taking from London banks pulled it back.
Several forex traders at leading banks said the Reserve Bank had been conspicuous by its absence.
"I expect the rand to continue softer tomorrow until the (central) bank steps in decisively," one said.
At the local close, the unit was at 4.5880/5910 against the dollar -- which came off its highs on international markets -- and from 4.5725/5755 overnight.
Other traders noted that there had been large speculative flows on the day and most expected another skittish session on Wednesday.
In cross rate action, the rand was last at 7.4753/4848 versus sterling from 7.4770/4864.
Against the mark the local unit was last changing hands at 0.3987/3992 from 0.4035/4039 Monday. It was fetching 25.6533/6810 against the yen from a previous level of 25.6999/7277.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 7.234 billion rand on Monday from 7.345 billion rand on Saturday.
On the money market, offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at 15.55 percent, while the 90-day BA rate also lined up unchanged at 15.00 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
